_: Written by `ci-video narrate`. Records which line each mp3 is a read of, in which voice, on which engine, at what prosody — so a later edit to any of those can be detected instead of silently keeping the old recording. Commit this with the mp3s.

one-config-each.text: Claude, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, OpenCode, VS Code. Each keeps its own settings, its own providers and its own list of tools.

copying-copies-keys.text: The obvious fix is to copy the files between machines. That can carry your API keys along with them.

title-card.text: CI Agent Sync is a portable map for every agent. Provider routes, tool bundles and workflows live in one store you can read, version and review.

first-run.text: It opens as a small web wizard on your own machine. Six steps, and it listens on loopback only.

vault.text: Credential values stay in 1Password. The wizard hands you two commands to run, and never asks you to paste a key.

agents.text: Pick the agents you use. Eleven are covered, from Claude and Codex to Hermes, OpenClaw and VS Code. Their sessions stay where they are.

profile.text: Then a working profile: CEO, engineering or marketing. It picks the reviewed bundles and the fallback chain, and leaves native app state alone.

generate.text: Generating the config writes into an ignored folder inside the store. It does not touch what your agents have installed.

backup.text: Before anything moves, it can take a redacted backup of the configs on the machine. Credential values and native sessions are never copied.

ready.text: Then the command line takes over. Doctor checks the machine, and sync shows a plan before it changes anything.

what-stays-yours.text: Policy travels. Credentials stay in your vault, and sessions stay on each machine. Every write waits for your approval.

close.text: CI Agent Sync, from Companion Intelligence. UnCloud your life.
